Subject: Demo recap + recommended models / benchmark links

Hi Sam — great to meet you and the FinTechX team today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call:

Summary of needs
- High-throughput invoice parsing & entity extraction (batched API calls)
- 99th percentile latency SLO around 200ms for request sizes ~1k tokens
- Strong semantic similarity/embedding for duplicate detection
- Tight cost targets for production (target cost < $0.002/token equivalent)

Recommended model fit (initial)
- Redwood-7B-quant: balanced latency/cost for conversational + extraction workloads (good baseline)
- Llama-2-13B-8bit (server-side): for higher-quality extraction where accuracy gains matter — expect ~2-3x cost vs 7B but higher recall
- Redwood-3B-quant: use for large-scale embedding/cheap reranking passes

Benchmark / evals we will provide
- Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS, p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies) for the models above — linked below
- Prompt set & example evals used for the FinTechX bench (attached: fintechx_prompt_set_v1.json)
- Initial benchmark report template we’ll fill out after your approval to run a smoke test

Next steps
1) I’ll drop the perf dashboard and prompt set in this thread (links + attachments).
2) If you’re good, can we schedule a 1-hour smoke bench next week to run your sample workload? I suggest Wed 6/23 or Thu 6/24.
3) Dylan will follow up on recommended runtime configs (batch sizes, KV cache hints, quantization knobs) after you pick a slot.

Attachments: fintechx_prompt_set_v1.json (application/json), redwood_verified_profiles.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks — looking forward to the bench.

On Thu, Jun 18, 2026 at 1:02 PM Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@fintechx.com> wrote:
> Thanks Alex — that all looks useful. A couple quick questions before we schedule the bench:
> 1) For Redwood-7B-quant, what TPS can you sustain and what does the p99 latency look like for payloads ~1k tokens?
> 2) Can you confirm whether embeddings are handled by the same runtime or a separate endpoint?

Great questions — summarized answers and links below. Seen also attached: benchmark_report_FX_20260618.pdf (smoke template + expected ranges).

Redwood-7B-quant (typical perf) — baseline numbers (single dedicated GPU, optimized kernels):
- Sustained TPS (small requests / concurrent clients): ~40–70 TPS depending on batching policy and token fan-out.
- Latency percentiles (1k token payloads, conservative batching to meet SLOs): p50 ~80–120ms, p90 ~120–180ms, p95 ~160–220ms, p99 ~240–350ms.
- Notes: p99 depends heavily on request coalescing and KV cache hit rate; for strict p99 SLOs we recommend dedicated capacity + conservative batching and prefix caching.

Embeddings: separate optimized path/endpoints — embeddings use a dedicated runtime path with batching tuned for small-fixed-length inputs. Embedding calls are charged / measured separately; however we can collocate them on the same Dedicated pool if you want to simplify routing.

Recommended starter config for your SLOs (99th < 200ms target):
- Dedicated pool with 2 GPUs (initial), enable prefix caching, max_batch_size=64, target_coalescing_latency_ms=10
- Use Redwood-7B-quant for extraction; escalate to Llama-2-13B-8bit for specific high-recall flows (e.g., OCR correction)

Links & resources (Redwood-verified)
- Perf dashboard (FinTechX view): https://dash.redwood.com/perf/FX-2026-0421 — contains TPS/latency percentiles for each model variant
- Verified profiles PDF (attached): redwood_verified_profiles.pdf
- Bench folder (prompt sets & raw outputs): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-fintechx-benchmarks

I’ve tentatively blocked Wed 6/23 at 10:00 AM PT for the smoke bench. Dylan — can you run the smoke config and share the bench command and expected runtime logs?

Attachments: benchmark_report_FX_20260618.pdf
